title: Show the controls when the task needs them.
intro: Build / Compose and Motion / Camera tabs helped me explore the system in an early executable prototype. But they also asked creators to understand the organization of the tool before making a simple edit.
I moved toward a contextual interface: select an object to inspect it, explicitly enter path editing to work on movement, and open Film Preview when it is time to assemble the sequence.

body: The default stage keeps attention on the scene. Path editing and the assembled film reveal their own timelines.

blocks.label: WHAT I KEPT
blocks.text: The underlying power stays. The permanent interface gets smaller.

body: The same distinction mattered in the monitor: checking another camera’s view should not silently replace a shot’s camera. I kept preview and editing intent separate so that exploration did not become an accidental change.
